source_evidence: ETF investors can trade their shares on the market at the market price whenever the market is open—minus any fees.
answer: ETF shares can be bought and sold on an exchange during market hours, typically through a brokerage account. Their trading price is not necessarily the same as the ETF’s net asset value (NAV), which reflects the value of its underlying holdings. The market price may be above NAV (a premium) or below NAV (a discount), so you might pay more or receive less than NAV when trading. Fees may also apply.
